en: Theragāthā 16.9 Vīsatinipāta Paṭhamavagga **Thera 169: Sāḷha** I have crossed over the flood; I am free from craving. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell in peace. My mind is well-liberated; I am one who has reached the goal. I am a bhikkhu who has lived the holy life. I have no more birth; this is my last body. I have attained the destruction of all suffering. I have realized the state of peace, the coolness, The unconditioned, the deathless, the island, The refuge, the shelter, the ultimate goal. I have reached the end of all suffering. The Verses of the Elder Anuruddha:
“Having abandoned mother and father,
sisters, kinsmen, and brothers;”
Having abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Anuruddha meditates alone,
yet he is accompanied by song and dance.
Awakened by the beating of drums,
he did not attain purity through that,
being delighted in the realm of Māra.
Having transcended this and delighting in the Buddha’s teaching,
having transcended the entire flood—
Only Anuruddha meditates.
Forms, sounds, tastes, smells,
and delightful tangibles— these do not disturb him.
Having transcended these,
Anuruddha alone meditates;
he has transcended the search for alms-food.
The sage, alone and without a second,
Anuruddha, free from taints, seeks out rag-robes.
The wise sage took the rag-robes, washed them, dyed them, and wore them.
Anuruddha is free from taints.
But he who has great desire and is discontented,
who is socially attached and agitated—
These qualities belong to him:
they are evil and defiling;
yet he is mindful and of few desires.
Contented and free from distress,
delighting in solitude and satisfied,
he is always one whose energy is aroused.
These wholesome factors conducive to enlightenment belong to him,
and he becomes one who is free from taints.
Thus it was said by the Great Seer:
"Having understood my intention,
the Teacher, the unsurpassed one in the world,"
By means of his mind-made body,
he approached through supernormal power.
When this thought arose in me:
Beyond that he taught:
the Buddha, delighting in the unproliferated,
taught the unproliferated.
Having understood his Dhamma,
I dwelt delighting in the teaching;
the three true knowledges were attained.
Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
For fifty-five years,
ever since I became one who never lies down to sleep;
For twenty-five years,
since drowsiness was utterly abandoned,
there have been for me no inhalations or exhalations.
For the one of such a nature whose mind is established,
free from passion, having undertaken peace—
the Visionary has attained final Nibbāna.
With a mind undaunted,
he endured the sensation;
like the extinguishing of a lamp, [he attained Nibbāna].
There arose a liberation of mind.
These were now the last for the Sage,
with contact as the fifth;
No other teachings shall remain once the Perfectly Enlightened One has attained final nibbāna;
there is now no further dwelling.
Within the ensnaring body of a god,
the wandering through births has been exhausted;
now there is no further becoming.
He who in a single moment has discerned the world in its thousandfold aspects, including the Brahma-world;
he who is a master of the qualities of psychic power regarding death and rebirth—
At the proper time, that bhikkhu beholds the deities.
Formerly, I was Annabhāra,
a poor man who carried fodder.
I attended upon the illustrious ascetic Upāriṭṭha;
for I was born in the Sakya clan.
"The wise know me as Anuruddha,
who was devoted to dancing and singing,
and was awakened by the rhythmic clapping of hands."
Then I saw the Perfectly Enlightened One,
the Teacher from whom there is no fear;
having inspired confidence in my heart toward him,
I went forth into the homeless life.
I know my former dwellings,
where I lived in the past.
Among the Tāvatiṁsa devas,
I stood as one born of Sakka’s lineage;
seven times, I was a lord of men.
I exercised sovereignty as a king;
victorious on all four sides,
I was the lord of the Jambusaṇḍa continent.
Without rod or sword,
I governed by the Dhamma;
seven [generations] from here and seven from there.
I shall remember fourteen rounds of existence,
while remaining then in the world of the gods.
In the five-factored concentration,
peaceful and unified,
attained through the subsiding of the hindrances—
My divine eye was purified;
I know the passing away and rebirth of beings,
their coming and going.
Established in the five-factored jhāna, he perceives existence as it is and as it becomes elsewhere.
The Teacher has been fully served by me.
... and the conduit to existence has been uprooted—
at Veḷuva Village among the Vajjis.
"At the end of my life,
beneath the bamboo grove,
I shall attain parinibbāna, free from all taints."
… the Elder Anuruddha …
